property_summary: For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for IAccessControl.interfaceId regardless of whether the contract also supports the IERC165 interfaceId, but the bug makes it return false when super.supportsInterface returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals IAccessControl's interfaceId, but the bug makes it additionally require super.supportsInterface to be true, causing it to return false for IAccessControl.interfaceId alone.

For any bytes4 `id`, `c.supportsInterface(id)` must return true iff `id == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || c.supportsInterface_erc165(id)`, but the mutant erroneously requires both conditions, returning false for `IAccessControl.interfaceId` when the contract does not support `IERC165`.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for IAccessControl's ID regardless of the ERC165 base result; the bug incorrectly ANDs both conditions, causing a false return for IAccessControl.interfaceId.
For any bytes4 `id`, `supportsInterface(id)` must return `true` for `IAccessControl.interfaceId` regardless of the IERC165 base result, but the mutant returns `false` due to ANDing both checks.
c.supportsInterface should return true for both IAccessControl and IERC165, but the mutant returns false for IERC165 because it skips the super call.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for IERC165 if it returns true for IAccessControl, but the mutant violates this by removing the super call, causing false for IERC165.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl, it must also return true for IERC165 because the inherited ERC165 base supports IERC165 and the super call chains; the mutant breaks this by skipping the super call and returning false for IERC165 even when IAccessControl is supported.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl, it must also return true for IERC165; the mutant violates this by removing the super call, causing supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) to return false.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl, it must also return true for IERC165 because the inherited ERC165 guarantees IERC165 support; the mutant breaks this by removing the super call and returning false for type(IERC165).interfaceId.

For any valid interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true if and only if the id matches IAccessControl or any interface it extends (ERC165). The bug violates this by returning false for IAccessControl, instead treating it as if only ERC165 is supported.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and correctly for type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the mutant only returns true for IERC165, flipping the expected result for IAccessControl.
For every bytes4 `interfaceId`, `supportsInterface` must return `true` when `interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId`; the mutant returns `false` for that same input.
For every bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for that input because it checks IERC165 instead of IAccessControl.

For any input bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals either type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant incorrectly returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.
For any role and account, the result of hasRole must match the internal roles mapping, but the mutant always returns true.
For any role and account, hasRole returns true if and only if the account was previously granted the role (the correct contract respects role assignments; the buggy always returns false).

For any role and account, if the role's admin (which can be obtained via getRoleAdmin) grants the role to the account, then hasRole must return true for that role and account; the reference honors the grant, while the buggy version always returns false.
For any role and any account, hasRole must return the same boolean value as the stored membership after a successful grant or direct assignment, but the buggy version always returns false.

For any role and account, if hasRole returns false for the role then after a self-renounce of the role the hasRole status must remain false, but in the reference code renounceRole can change a true state to false while the buggy version always returns false, so the rule holds for the reference and is trivially met but vacuously invariant; instead: after granting a role to an account via grantRole (with proper admin), hasRole must return true for that account; the reference returns true, the buggy version always false.

The hasRole function must consistently reflect the actual stored membership; the bugged version always returns the logical negation, so for any role and account, the reference returns the membership flag while the mutant returns its opposite.
For any role and account that has been granted the role, hasRole must return true; the mutant inverts the stored membership, returning false for granted roles.
For any role and any account, calling hasRole(role, account) returns the same boolean as the stored membership, but the mutant returns the negation.
For any granted role, hasRole must return true; the mutant inverts the return, causing hasRole to return false for an account that actually possesses the role.

For the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE role, the initial deployer (address(this)) is a member after construction, so hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, address(this)) must return true; the mutant inverts the boolean and returns false.

The `hasRole` function should return the actual membership stored for the requested role; the bug makes it always return membership for `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, so for any non-DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE role where an account’s membership differs from its DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE membership, the returned values diverge.

For any role and account, the hasRole function must return the stored membership for that specific role; the bug instead returns the membership of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, so for any non-zero role where the account's membership differs from its DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE membership, the values diverge.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) must return the same boolean as the membership stored for that role; the mutant instead returns the membership of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, causing divergence whenever the account's membership differs between the requested role and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) must return the membership of that account for that exact role; the mutant always returns the membership for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, violating this when the account's membership differs between the requested role and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.

For any non-DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE role R and account A, hasRole(R, A) must equal the R-specific membership; the bug returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE membership, causing divergence when A's membership differs between R and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
For any role and account, if the role has been granted to the account via the contract's own grantRole, then hasRole must return true; the mutant always returns false, breaking this rule.
